cancer_indication: Hormone receptor–positive, HER2-negative breast cancer (in combination with endocrine therapy for adjuvant therapy in stage II–III early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence, and for advanced/metastatic disease with an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant).
moa: Ribociclib is a selective inhibitor of CDK4 and CDK6, kinases that bind D-type cyclins and drive G1→S cell-cycle progression. By inhibiting CDK4/6, ribociclib prevents phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma protein (RB1), keeping RB1 in its hypophosphorylated, E2F-bound state and blocking E2F-mediated transcription required for the G1/S transition. This results in G1 cell-cycle arrest and reduced proliferation, and clinically deeper suppression of proliferation markers (e.g., Ki-67) when combined with endocrine therapy in HR+/HER2− breast cancer.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Represents transcriptional programs driven by E2F that enable S-phase entry and DNA replication, regulated by RB1 phosphorylation status.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: E2F-driven proliferation programs are central to HR+/HER2− breast cancer growth; suppressing E2F output via the CDK4/6–RB1 checkpoint is a key determinant of disease control with ribociclib-based therapy.

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Encompasses genes controlling progression through G2 and mitosis, including mitotic regulators that rise in proliferating tumors.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation: G2/M activity reflects high proliferative throughput in breast cancer; downstream mitotic programs diminish when upstream G1/S entry is blocked, linking this pathway to tumor proliferation state.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: A growth and survival signaling axis that promotes proliferation and anti-apoptotic programs downstream of PI3K and AKT through mTOR.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling provides alternative growth and survival inputs in breast cancer and can reduce dependence on CDK4/6-mediated cell-cycle control, shaping therapeutic benefit and failure patterns.

HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.description: Captures activation of MAPK/ERK-related signaling programs often driven by upstream receptor and growth-factor signaling inputs.
HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.interpretation: MAPK/ERK-linked signaling can sustain proliferative signaling in breast cancer and contribute to reduced reliance on CDK4/6–RB1 gating, affecting durability of response to CDK4/6 inhibition.

REACTOME_CYCLIN_E_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_DURI.description: Represents Cyclin E–linked events controlling late G1 to S-phase entry and related transcriptional and replication programs.
REACTOME_CYCLIN_E_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_DURI.interpretation: Cyclin E/CDK2 activity can provide an alternative route to RB1 phosphorylation and S-phase entry in breast cancer, influencing how strongly tumors depend on cyclin D–CDK4/6 control.

WU_APOPTOSIS_BY_CDKN1A_VIA_TP53.description: Reflects TP53–CDKN1A (p21) checkpoint signaling that can reinforce cell-cycle arrest and is discussed in the context of CDK4/6 inhibitor response.
WU_APOPTOSIS_BY_CDKN1A_VIA_TP53.interpretation: TP53–p21 checkpoint integrity is relevant to breast cancer control under CDK4/6 inhibition because p21 levels correlate with ribociclib sensitivity and loss of this checkpoint is linked to reduced enforcement of arrest.

REACTOME_ABERRANT_REGULATION_OF_MITOTIC_.description: Represents dysregulated G1/S control caused by RB1 defects, disrupting the RB1–E2F checkpoint that normally constrains S-phase entry.
REACTOME_ABERRANT_REGULATION_OF_MITOTIC_.interpretation: RB1 defects undermine the central mechanistic node targeted by CDK4/6 inhibitors in breast cancer, limiting the ability of ribociclib to induce durable G1 arrest and thereby shaping intrinsic and acquired non-response.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High CDK4 expression (with relatively low CDK6) is described as correlating with extreme sensitivity to ribociclib, consistent with dependence on CDK4/6-mediated G1/S control.
Higher p21 (CDKN1A) levels correlate with ribociclib sensitivity and reinforce G1 arrest; loss of p21 is described in resistant models.
Cyclin D1 amplification/overexpression is described as common in HR+ tumors and linked to dependence on CDK4/6 activity, yielding pronounced arrest with CDK4/6 inhibition.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Low CDK6 is described as part of a high-CDK4/low-CDK6 expression pattern associated with heightened ribociclib sensitivity, while CDK6 overexpression is linked to resistance.
Lower Cyclin E1 activity (absence of CCNE1 amplification) is described as favoring response, whereas increased Cyclin E1/CDK2 activity bypasses CDK4/6 dependence.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: CDK6 amplification/overexpression is described as a resistance mechanism, enabling reduced dependence on CDK4-directed control despite CDK4/6 inhibition.
CCNE1 amplification/overactivity is described as driving Cyclin E/CDK2-mediated RB1 phosphorylation, bypassing CDK4/6 inhibition and correlating with poorer outcomes.
Upregulation of the Cyclin E/CDK2 axis is described as a bypass mechanism that can phosphorylate RB1 independently of CDK4/6.
p16 (CDKN2A) upregulation/amplification is described in the context of RB pathway disruption and resistance, particularly when RB1 function is compromised.
PI3K pathway activation (including PIK3CA mutations) is described as enriched in CDK4/6 inhibitor–resistant tumors and as providing alternative survival/proliferation signaling.
FGFR1 amplification is described as an upstream activator of PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK signaling, contributing to reduced dependence on CDK4/6 control and resistance.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss of functional RB1 is described as the most definitive resistance mechanism because CDK4/6 inhibitors require intact RB1 to enforce G1 arrest.
Downregulation/loss of p21 (CDKN1A) is described in resistant models and is linked to reduced enforcement of G1 arrest under CDK4/6 inhibition.
Reduced p53–p21 checkpoint activity (e.g., via TP53 mutation) is described as undermining G1 arrest and contributing to resistance.
Loss of ER signaling is described in some resistant metastatic lesions where ER expression falls, reducing hormone-driven cyclin D dependence and thereby diminishing CDK4/6 inhibitor sensitivity.
PTEN loss is described as part of PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation patterns enriched in CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance, supporting bypass survival/proliferation signaling.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Luminal A (HR+/HER2−, low proliferation): These tumors generally respond well to ribociclib + endocrine therapy, often achieving durable disease control; markers of high CDK4/cyclin D1 and intact Rb are described as common.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Luminal B (HR+/HER2−, higher proliferati: These tumors are more proliferative and are described as deriving greater absolute benefit from CDK4/6 inhibition; in CORALLEEN (luminal B), ribociclib+letrozole markedly suppressed proliferation compared to chemotherapy, and immune gene signatures in luminal B were specifically dampened by ribociclib.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-positive (HER2+/HR−): Ribociclib is described as not approved for HER2+ disease; early-phase combinations with anti-HER2 therapy (in HR+/HER2+) suggest some activity, but effects in HER2+/HR− tumors are described as unproven with no formal indication.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-negative (HR−/HER2−): TNBC is described as generally not benefiting from CDK4/6 inhibitors; many TNBC have RB loss or low RB activity and rely on CDK2/E2F or other pathways, and basal-like models show minimal response in preclinical data; not recommended outside trials.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA-mutated or HRD-positive: No indication is described that BRCA status predicts ribociclib efficacy; PARP inhibitors, not CDK4/6 inhibitors, are described as the targeted therapy in BRCA-driven breast cancer.
